$comment: Frontira brand identity contract (#60). General, not Open Graph scoped: the OG contract (assets/open-graph/contract.json) describes one canvas, and every other brand-bearing surface — app headers and footers, auth screens, document covers, presentation bookends, wallpapers — had no contract at all. That is what let a consumer set the official F beside a TYPESET 'frontira' and call it the identity.

brand.$comment: The name is lowercase everywhere it is written as prose (assets/brand/writing.json). The MARK is a graphic and keeps its drawn form.
brand.cvp: Liberating intelligent people from unintelligent work
brand.cvpNote: Settled 2026-07-25 and binding here: the CVP is a claim, not a sentence, and a claim that changes shape per market is not a claim. A German surface sets its headline and chrome in German and leaves the CVP untranslated.

variants.$comment: Three, and the third is a composition rather than a file. There is no mark-plus-wordmark asset because the F mark IS the wordmark's own first glyph — measured, both carry an identical 14.87% monoline stroke — so setting them side by side prints the same F twice.

mark.note: The lettermark alone. It does not say the company's name, which is why the surface matrix restricts where it may stand in for the identity.

wordmark.note: The default on brand-bearing surfaces. The name comes from the drawing, never from type.

lockup.note: The wordmark asset above the CVP, typeset in the brand grotesque. The NAME is still the official drawing; only the CVP is type, and the CVP is a sentence rather than the brand name, so setting it is not an approximation of anything.
lockup.cvpMaxWidthNote: The CVP block is bounded by the wordmark's own rendered width, so the lockup stays one rectangle instead of a wordmark with a paragraph trailing off it.

surfaces.$comment: The matrix that makes the header/footer and compact-icon decision deterministic, which is the acceptance criterion. `requires` is the minimum identity the surface must carry: a surface requiring `name` refuses the mark, because the mark does not say who this is.

appHeader.note: the primary identity of a running application

authScreen.note: a sign-in screen is exactly where a user checks who they are handing credentials to

favicon.note: 16px of square: the wordmark cannot survive it

narrowNav.note: a collapsed rail, where the wordmark would be clipped rather than small

minimalSignature.note: a deliberately quiet corner signature on a surface whose identity is already established elsewhere

typesetApproximation.$comment: THE RULE #60 EXISTS FOR, and the one that has to be machine-checkable rather than advisory. Inside an identity slot the name is a drawing. Text spelling the brand name in that slot is an approximation of the wordmark however carefully it is styled, and it is the observed failure: the official F beside a typeset 'frontira'.
typesetApproximation.rule: An identity slot contains the official asset geometry. Text spelling the brand name inside an identity slot is a violation, whatever font it is set in.
typesetApproximation.proseNote: Running copy may write frontira as often as it likes — that is the writing contract's business, not this one. The distinction is the slot: prose NAMES the company, an identity slot IS the company.
typesetApproximation.standaloneFBesideName: The mark may sit beside prose that mentions the brand. It may not sit beside a typeset name acting as the identity — that composition is the lockup, and the lockup takes its name from the asset.

clearSpace.$comment: Half the mark's width, on all four sides, scaled with the rendered identity rather than fixed in pixels.
clearSpace.factorNote: half the mark's aspect (0.578 / 2), so clear space is expressed against the rendered HEIGHT, which is the dimension every variant shares.

contrast.$comment: An identity is not decoration, so it is held to the 4.5:1 text floor rather than the 3:1 graphical-object floor. This is why the register-aware asset exists: the official wordmark is hardcoded #6F43D5, which measures 6.11:1 on paper but only 3.24:1 on ink #0A0A0F and 3.03:1 on ink raised.
contrast.floorRationale: the identity is read, not glanced at

ink.note: the wordmark follows currentColor, so on ink it takes the register's own text colour at 17.64:1

paper.note: purple on white is 6.11:1 and is the brand's own colour

geometry.$comment: Pinned so a redrawn or re-exported asset cannot pass as the brand. Hashes are of the official path data alone, so a fill or an accessible name may change without breaking consumers.
geometry.hardFloorNote: measured: below 11px the monoline stroke falls under 1.5 device pixels and the letterforms break. Every minHeightPx above sits over this floor.

accessibility.nameNote: The identity carries its name for assistive technology. The official files ship a <title> but no role, so the derived assets add role=img and aria-label — a logo exposed as decorative tells a screen reader the page belongs to nobody.
accessibility.decorativeException: A second, repeated instance of the identity on the same surface may be aria-hidden, so the name is not announced twice.
